locator.section: Limitation of the concept of radical/charge-site initiation

evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.33 draws the full cyclohexane decomposition as a charge-site pathway: neutral cyclohexane --(-e-)--> cyclohexane radical cation (drawn as an intact ring bearing '+.') --(sigma)--> ring-opened 1,6-distonic hexyl radical cation (ring drawn open on the right side, radical '.' on one terminus and '+' on the other) --(i)--> product. Only the ENCODED step (the 'i', inductive/charge-site cleavage) carries a drawn electron arc. The ionization and the sigma ring-opening are NOT encoded because the intact C6H12 molecular ion cannot be given a localized RDKit-parseable SMILES (a closed ring with all 12 H is neutral closed-shell; its '+.' is a delocalized 2-centre-1-electron sigma hole), so the mechanism is encoded starting from the ring-opened distonic hexyl radical cation that the '+.'/'.' arc actually acts on; that species is an isomer of the cyclohexane M+. (both C6H12, m/z 84). Book draws 1 arc (a double-barbed, 2-electron curved arrow whose tail sits on the C4-C5 sigma bond and whose head points at the C5-C6 bond); move <1> is exactly that drawn arrow. No implicit homolysis hook is needed: the charge-site inductive cleavage is a single 2-electron heterolytic process (C4-C5 bonding pair shifts to form the C5=C6 pi bond of ethylene, charge migrates C6->C4). The page prints no m/z or intensity for THIS (cyclohexane) scheme; the adjacent text mentions a 'substantial peak at m/z 56' but attributes it to the spectrum of 2-methyl[pentane], not to the drawn cyclohexane scheme.

Equation 8.33 has NO dedicated MØD rule (rule_index by_equation['8.33'] is null). The text cross-references Equation 4.30 (the radical-site analog of the same cyclic-ion decomposition), whose rule is IMS_4_30 with DFS [C.]1[C]2[C]3[C+]4[C]5{=}[C]6>>[C.]1[C+]2.[C]3{=}[C]4[C]5{=}[C]6. CROSS-LINK VERIFIED AS A MISMATCH: IMS_4_30 operates on a different substrate (a hexadienyl distonic ion already bearing a C5=C6 double bond and a remote C4 cation), cleaves the C2-C3 bond, and expels butadiene (C3=C4-C5=C6) to leave an ionized-ethylene fragment (C1.-C2+, m/z 28). Scheme 8.33's drawn 'i' step instead starts from an all-single-bond 1,6-distonic hexyl ion, cleaves C4-C5, forms C5=C6, and expels neutral ethylene to leave the C4H8+. ion at m/z 56. Different substrate, different cleaved bond, different products -> IMS_4_30 does NOT encode this scheme and is recorded in rule_mismatches.
